title: Governed AI Architecture & Secure Implementation
short: Build an agent with approved access and security boundaries.
summary: Design and build an AI agent for an agreed task. Record its approved purpose, scope, accountable owner, and review conditions, then enforce and test identity, data, and tool boundaries.
problem: A demonstration can work while leaving unclear who approved the agent’s purpose, what it can reach or change, how it handles malicious instructions, and who responds when a control fails.
examine: Applications, workflows, data sources, and existing AI usage
User, application, and agent identities
Threat paths through retrieved content, connected tools, and delegated access
Limits on connecting systems and responsibilities for running them
change: Record the agent’s purpose, permitted actions, prohibitions, accountable owner, and review triggers
Map each agent identity to its permitted resources and actions
Connect models and tools through interfaces with explicit authorization and failure handling
Configure approval gates, activity records, monitoring, and ownership procedures
Test prompt injection, unauthorized access, blocked operations, and recovery paths
deliver: A system map and design showing identity, data, and tool paths
An authorization record and build plan with approved actions, prohibitions, approval points, owner, and dependencies
Working integrations, security test results for allowed and blocked actions, and operating instructions

title: AI Governance & Security Assessment
short: Compare real system access and safeguards with intended use.
summary: Review AI tools and agents against their actual permissions, connected data, threat exposure, owners, release practices, and activity records. Receive prioritized findings and a technical remediation plan.
problem: Your AI policies may not match what the tools in use can actually access or do. Review whether identity, data, and tool controls contain risks such as prompt injection, excessive access, and unsafe actions.
examine: AI tools, agent identities, permissions, connected data, and tool operations
Exposure to prompt injection, sensitive-data disclosure, excessive authority, and unsafe actions
Owners, approvals for putting AI into use, activity records, and review schedules
Existing policies and how they map to configured controls
change: Identify security and governance gaps, and separate urgent exposure from longer-term changes
Name the people responsible for deciding which fixes to make
Define a practical implementation scope
deliver: Findings for company leaders, with the most important issues first
A map of technical safeguards, security observations, and the evidence behind each finding
Priorities for fixes and an agreed next step

title: Agent Governance & Security
short: Set and enforce an agent’s identity, access, and action limits.
summary: Record each agent’s approved purpose, permitted and prohibited actions, accountable owner, identity, approval conditions, and review triggers. Enforce least-privilege access, test misuse and denial paths, and prepare a removal process.
problem: An AI agent can read information and use tools to act. A prompt can be manipulated and a legitimate connector can still expose too much. Set enforceable limits, decide which actions need approval, and make access reviewable and revocable.
examine: Identity and authentication paths for each agent
Tool permissions, delegated access, resource boundaries, and excessive authority
How untrusted prompts and retrieved content could redirect actions or expose data
Named decision authority, accountable owner, approval conditions, review triggers, and retirement
change: Limit identity, tools, data, and operations to the approved task
Require review before external, financial, destructive, or difficult-to-reverse actions
Test malicious instructions, denied operations, failures, and access changes
Connect monitoring, access reviews, ownership changes, and offboarding
deliver: A signed or approved record of each agent’s purpose, scope, prohibitions, decision authority, and review conditions
Configured safeguards and security test cases
Responsibilities for monitoring, responding, reviewing, changing, and removing agent access

title: Microsoft AI Governance & Security
short: Trace governance and safeguards from content to agent action.
summary: Trace a defined workload through Copilot content permissions, Copilot Studio authentication, Entra agent identity, Purview evidence, and Power Platform environments. Review prompt-injection exposure, connector scope, and action controls, and record organizational authorization separately from product configuration.
problem: Microsoft controls can configure and record access, but they do not decide an agent’s business purpose, prohibited actions, approving authority, or review conditions for your organization.
examine: SharePoint and OneDrive permissions, Copilot discovery, labels, and source data
Copilot Studio authentication choices, connectors, makers, and environment policies
Entra agent identity, Purview records, Power Platform boundaries, and the organizational authorization decision
change: Map approved purpose, owner, prohibitions, approval conditions, and external effects to Microsoft configuration
Review source permissions, credential context, connectors, prompt protections, and environment boundaries
Implement agreed tenant-specific changes and test authorized actions, injection scenarios, and denials
deliver: A workload map connecting organizational authorization to Microsoft identities, data, tools, and evidence
Prioritized security and governance changes with verification results
An authorization record with named approval and operating owners, review conditions, and records to retain

title: Secure AI Integration & Legacy Modernization
short: Expose approved business actions through a controlled interface.
summary: Connect AI to older applications through APIs that check identity and permissions, expose only approved operations, record activity, and handle failures safely.
problem: Useful business information often sits in older applications and disconnected processes. A direct AI connection can bypass access rules, expose sensitive records, or allow an unsafe action to propagate when something fails.
examine: Legacy application interfaces and integration dependencies
Data access patterns, authorization, and failure handling
Hosting, deployment, maintenance, and migration constraints
change: Create APIs with identity checks, least-privilege access, and clear rules for permitted operations
Improve system connections and selected parts of older applications
Connect AI features with approval steps, audit records, and a process for containing unexpected results
deliver: Integration and modernization plan
Tested system connections and working workflows
Migration, recovery, and maintenance guidance

title: Platform Engineering & Technical Operations
short: Keep the application and release path maintainable.
summary: Build and maintain Next.js applications, integrations, and release processes. Document deployment, routine operations, and recovery so the platform can be handed over clearly.
problem: A platform needs more than a launch. Deployment, content architecture, integrations, maintenance, and recovery must remain understandable as the system changes.
examine: Application architecture, hosting, and deployment process
Content and integration requirements
Performance constraints and ongoing maintenance needs
change: Build or improve Next.js applications and integration layers
Establish reproducible deployment and maintenance workflows
Use AI-assisted development with human review and verification
deliver: Working platform and integration changes
Deployment and recovery documentation
An agreed technical operations scope

title: Governance & Security Remediation
summary: Fix the access, identity, data boundary, activity-record, and ongoing management issues found in an assessment. Test the changes and document remaining risks.
problem: An assessment may identify problems your team still needs to fix. Agree on who will make the changes, what the work includes, and how to test that the fixes work.
examine: Assessment findings and affected systems
Dependencies, accountable owners, and change constraints
Current configuration and verification evidence
change: Apply least-privilege permission, identity, and data-boundary changes
Implement approval, monitoring, incident response, inventory, and lifecycle controls
Update integrations and operating procedures
deliver: Completed changes and test results for expected, denied, and failure behavior
An updated map of safeguards and instructions for running the system
Remaining risks and a handover plan
